0.long_answer: According to the World Health Organization (WHO) classification, the diagnosis of acute myeloid leukemia (AML) is made when more than 20% of the blood or bone marrow is composed of myeloblasts, except in specific cases with certain recurrent genetic abnormalities. For minimally differentiated acute myeloblastic leukemia (M0), when no such genetic abnormalities are present, the minimum blast percentage required to diagnose AML is over 20%. This criterion distinguishes AML from other hematologic disorders and is the current standard for cases without defining genetic markers.
